extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners involved in observational epidemiology (authors of cohort/case–control/cross-sectional studies), systematic reviewers, journal editors, and guideline users
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating and applying the STROBE reporting recommendations for observational studies (cohort, case–control, cross-sectional), including distinguishing appropriate uses (guiding reporting) from inappropriate uses (assessing study quality or guiding study design/conduct).

rubrics_metrics.name: STROBE checklist (22 items)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology (STROBE) recommendations consist of a checklist of 22 items that provide guidance on the reporting of cohort, case–control and cross-sectional studies, in order to facilitate critical appraisal and interpretation of results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the full 22-item STROBE checklist when reporting observational studies to ensure complete transparent reporting that facilitates appraisal and interpretation. The checklist is specifically for reporting; it does not itself assess methodological quality or prescribe how to design or conduct studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate use: guide reporting of observational studies
rubrics_metrics.description: The use of STROBE to guide the reporting of observational studies was considered appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When authors prepare manuscripts of cohort, case–control, or cross-sectional studies, they should use STROBE to check that all key reporting elements are present. In the study sample, among 32 observational studies that cited STROBE, 26 (81%) made appropriate use in this reporting role — this is the intended and correct application of the checklist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inappropriate use: using STROBE to assess methodological quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Inappropriate uses included the use of STROBE as a tool to assess the methodological quality of studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use the STROBE reporting checklist as a risk-of-bias or methodological-quality assessment tool in systematic reviews or meta-analyses; STROBE items address reporting completeness, not internal validity. The paper found frequent misuse of STROBE in this way: among 19 systematic reviews in the sample, 10 (53%) used STROBE inappropriately to assess study quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inappropriate use: using STROBE as guidance for study design or conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Inappropriate uses included the use of STROBE as a guideline on how to design and conduct studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: STROBE should not be interpreted as methodological guidance for planning or conducting studies; it focuses on what to report after a study is done. Researchers and reviewers should use appropriate design/methodology guidance (e.g., methodological textbooks, design-specific guidance) rather than STROBE for planning or conducting research.
